title: Silky Dark Chocolate Fudge Squares
summary: Rich dark chocolate fudge made in minutes by melting chocolate with condensed milk and butter, then chilling until firm enough to cut into neat squares.
equipment: saucepan that the bowl sits on snugly

ingredients.note: check the label; many contain soya lecithin or traces of milk

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, cubed, plus a little for the tin
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Line the tin
steps.text: Rub the tin with a little butter and line it with baking paper, leaving paper hanging over two opposite sides so you can lift the fudge out later.

steps.title: Melt gently
steps.text: Put the chocolate, condensed milk, butter and salt into the heatproof bowl and set it over a pan of barely simmering water, making sure the base stays clear of the water. Stir for 4-6 min, until just a few small lumps of chocolate are left.

steps.title: Stir until smooth
steps.text: Take the bowl off the pan and keep stirring; the leftover heat melts the last pieces and the mixture turns thick and glossy. Stir in the vanilla.

steps.title: Chill to set
steps.text: Scrape the fudge into the tin, smooth the top and refrigerate uncovered for at least 3 h. It is ready when the centre feels firm, not tacky, when pressed with a fingertip.

steps.title: Cut into squares
steps.text: Lift the slab out using the paper and cut it into 36 squares with a large knife, wiping the blade clean between cuts for sharp edges.

tips: The most common mistake is overheating the chocolate; if the mixture turns oily or grainy, it got too hot, so take the bowl off while a few lumps remain.
Choose a chocolate with cocoa listed before sugar; very sweet chips give a soft fudge that will not slice cleanly.
For a little crunch, press a few chopped toasted hazelnuts or walnuts on top before chilling.
Let the squares stand at room temperature for 10 min before serving for the creamiest texture.
storage: Keep in an airtight box in the fridge for up to 2 weeks, with baking paper between layers, or freeze for up to 2 months.
